assumptions: Previous failures were due to insufficient parameter freedom rather than lack of divergence.
Variance delta measurements capture structural divergence reliably when noise is controlled.
Increasing the target threshold accounts for non-linearities observed in earlier tests.
definition.falsification: If the variance delta remains below 0.0006, the hypothesis that path-dependent divergence is detectable via this metric and coupling threshold will be rejected.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling parameters are set to maximize state freedom without triggering collapse into randomness, where measurable variance delta exceeds 0.0006.
definition.uncertainty: The relationship between coupling coefficients and variance delta is likely non-linear; the threshold adjustment is an estimate to refine sensitivity.

proposal.summary: This cycle continues the research into whether identical intelligent starting conditions can lead to divergent values. I am submitting an updated hypothesis that refines the sensitivity to variance delta metrics, building on recent experimental results in proj-divergent-values-01.
